commands.command: Design change: repopact_remote_provider::provider::RemoteRepositoryProvider::open_snapshot signature extended with a new SnapshotDownloadOptions { destination_path, max_compressed_bytes, should_cancel } parameter; SnapshotDescriptor gains owner_label/repository_name fields
commands.summary: Checkpoint A's original open_snapshot(&self, descriptor) could not support a caller-chosen staging destination, a compressed-byte bound enforced while streaming, or cancellation -- discovered as a real defect only once Checkpoint C had to stream a real multi-megabyte archive rather than stat a test fixture. Refined per the standing instruction to change Checkpoint A/B abstractions only where production integration proves a defect. FakeProvider and the provider_neutrality.rs integration test updated to the new signature and re-verified (GH-011 unaffected).

commands.command: New: repopact_mobile_acquisition::workspace::WorkspaceManager::import_remote_snapshot (+ normalize_single_root_directory helper); AcquisitionKind::RemoteSnapshot, distinct from WI068's reserved RemoteGit, reused from Checkpoint A/B
commands.summary: Reuses the exact same staging-then-publish transaction and the exact same, unmodified archive::import_archive as WI065's own SafArchive import path -- no second extractor. The only new step is an optional, purely-filesystem post-extraction promotion of a single top-level wrapper directory (GitHub zipballs always wrap in owner-repo-shortsha/), which runs strictly after import_archive's own zip-slip/symlink/bounds validation already accepted every path, so it cannot itself escape the workspace root or bypass any archive-security check. cargo test -p repopact-mobile-acquisition: 75/75 passed, including 5 new remote_snapshot_import_* tests: case-collision rejection, entry-count-bound rejection, malformed-archive rejection, credential-free-provenance publication, and single-root-directory stripping -- all leaving no ready workspace and no staging residue on failure.

commands.command: New: repopact_provider_github::transport::{StreamingDownloadTransport, StreamingRequest, StreamingDownloadOutcome} + ReqwestTransport::download (a second, longer-timeout blocking client; manual redirect loop reusing the exact same Decision 0061 Authorization-header allowlist logic as the REST GET path; streamed to disk in 256KB chunks via a bounded loop that checks should_cancel and the byte count every chunk; partial destination file removed on any error)
commands.summary: Deliberately does not reuse Checkpoint B's 8MB REST-JSON response ceiling (item Phase 5): a new SNAPSHOT_DOWNLOAD_MAX_COMPRESSED_BYTES = 300MiB bound is defined in the app layer, distinct from both that ceiling and from WI065's own ArchiveBounds::max_expanded_bytes (1GiB). Rejects an https-to-http redirect downgrade (checked only on redirect hops reached via a redirect, verified via a pure-function unit test plus real local-socket tests -- the original request's own scheme is never itself constrained, since production always builds https://api.github.com/... and this module's own tests intentionally use plain http://127.0.0.1 test servers end-to-end).

11 real local-socket tests, 0 failures: a successful streamed download to the destination file; a compressed-byte-bound rejection mid-stream with the partial file removed; cancellation (checked before the first read) leaving no partial file; a rejected 404; a rejected redirect with a missing Location header; a rejected connection-refused host; a rejected empty body; a pure-function proof that an https-original redirect downgrading to http is rejected while an already-http chain is not treated as a downgrade; and -- mirroring Checkpoint B's own successful pattern -- two independent local TCP servers proving on the wire that the Authorization header does not survive either a REST GET redirect or a download redirect to a non-allowlisted host.

commands.command: GitHubProvider::describe_snapshot/open_snapshot wired to the real zipball endpoint (GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/zipball/{sha}) and the new StreamingDownloadTransport; typed error mapping (map_download_error) for cancellation/oversized/401/403/404/429/protocol errors
commands.summary: The download URL is built entirely from the already-resolved typed descriptor (owner/name + the exact immutable commit SHA that produced the request) -- never from an archive filename, Content-Disposition header, or redirect target, and never accepted from a caller (Phase 9). cargo test -p repopact-provider-github provider::: unit tests prove the exact URL construction, that Authorization is attached only when actually connected (never for an unauthenticated/public request), and that download errors map to the correct typed ErrorCode (SnapshotTooLarge, DownloadCancelled). Full crate: 57 non-ignored tests passed, 5 ignored (live).

commands.command: New Tauri command: remote_import_snapshot (+ remote_import_cancel); apps/repopact-desktop/src-tauri/src/remote_provider.rs; registered in lib.rs invoke_handler and permissions/workbench.toml
commands.summary: Accepts only typed repository/ref identifiers (repositoryId/owner/name, displayName/kind/refId) -- no URL, header map, or filesystem destination is ever accepted from the frontend. The exact commit SHA is re-resolved natively inside this command from repository+reference, never trusted from any value the frontend already displayed (Phase 4/9/31 -- the frontend's RemoteRefRef DTO has no SHA field to even supply). Staging/download destinations are allocated entirely by the native backend under the same WorkspaceManager root Decision 0057 already specifies. A single active-import cancellation token (Mutex<Option<CancellationToken>>) rejects a second concurrent import attempt and is cancellable via the new remote_import_cancel command.
